title.en: John Oliver on police surveillance: ‘Big Brother on steroids’
title.zh: 约翰·奥利弗谈警方监控：‘加强版老大哥’

summary.en: John Oliver, host of Last Week Tonight, criticized police use of surveillance technologies such as cameras, microphones, and license plate readers, describing them as 'wildly invasive' tools for tracking Americans.
summary.zh: 《上周今夜》主持人约翰·奥利弗批评警方使用摄像头、麦克风和车牌识别器等监控技术，称这些工具“极具侵入性”，用于追踪美国民众。

body.en: Host tore into the ‘wildly invasive’ cameras, microphones and license plate readers that police use to track Americans John Oliver discussed the tools that police are using to keep track of Americans on the latest episode of Last Week Tonight. In recent years, the use of surveillance technology has exploded among local police forces due to decreasing prices and federal funding, with one local mayor comparing modern systems to “Big Brother on steroids.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 主持人深入剖析了警察用来追踪美国人的“极具侵入性”的摄像头、麦克风和车牌阅读器。约翰·奥利弗在最新一集的《上周今夜秀》中讨论了警方用来追踪美国人的工具。近年来，由于价格下降和联邦资金的增加，监控技术的使用在当地警察部队中呈爆炸式增长，一位当地市长将现代系统比作“类固醇的老大哥”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The increasing use of surveillance technology raises important questions about the balance between security and individual freedom. When unchecked, power can become overwhelming, potentially making citizens feel vulnerable rather than protected. Yahweh calls leaders to govern with justice, ensuring that authority serves the people, not oppresses them.
reflection.zh: 监控技术的日益普及引发了关于安全与个人自由之间平衡的重要问题。当权力不受制约时，它可能变得势不可挡，使公民感到脆弱而非受到保护。雅伟呼召领袖以公义治理，确保权力服务于人民，而非压迫人民。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Restore leader accuses Farage of ‘outright lying’ over pact offer but says his party ‘remains open’ – UK politics live
title.zh: 英国改革党动用海军阻止小型船只的承诺引来批评——政治直播

summary.en: Reform UK's proposal to use the Navy to intercept small boats carrying migrants has drawn criticism from Labour, who call it a distraction, and from a retired commander who deems it lacking substance. The issue of illegal migration has gained political prominence following a significant crossing into a Spanish enclave.
summary.zh: 英国改革党承诺动用海军阻止小型船只（载有移民）的计划受到批评。工党称此举是“转移对丑闻注意力的绝望尝试”，一位退休指挥官则认为其“缺乏实质”。自数万名摩洛哥人进入西班牙飞地以来，英国围绕非法移民的政策在政治上的重要性有所提升。

body.en: Rupert Lowe says no talks have taken place after the Reform UK leader said he was ‘open to conversation’ on some sort of electoral deal Zia Yusuf said under the plan Reform will create an “integrated surveillance command”, which he claims will “unify” military and intelligence surveillance, making “ours the most surveilled maritime border in the world”. “Any vessel attempting to cross illegally will be intercepted by our armed forces who will return them back to France,” he said, adding that emergency legislation would be given to the armed forces to equip them with the “necessary powers”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 工党称该计划是“绝望地试图分散注意力”，而一名退休指挥官则称该计划“缺乏实质内容” 自上周数万名摩洛哥人越境进入西班牙飞地休达以来，英国针对非法移民的政策的政治重要性有所上升，导致数十人死亡（包括溺水或被压死）并引发了马德里的政治危机。西班牙官员随后表示，几乎所有周四抵达休达的人都已返回。英国改革党内政事务发言人齐亚·优素福(Zia Yusuf)表示，该党的小船计划部分是受到他在休达所见所闻的启发。他今天早上告诉英国广播公司第四台“今日”节目：我看到士兵使用胡椒喷雾直接与行为不检的移民互动。通过使用军队，我看到西班牙能够在一天之内驱逐并有效遣返大约 40,000 名非法移民。我真诚地相信，我们两个运动可能有足够的共同点进行集体合作，摧毁迫在眉睫的左翼联盟，该联盟将终结这个国家仅存的希望。在我看来，因为我们个人的困难而不去尝试是不可行的。现在是抛开分歧，为了我们所热爱的国家的利益而合作的时候了。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Debates over national borders and migration often challenge societies to consider how they treat those seeking entry. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to welcome foreigners as if they were native-born, recalling our own shared human experience of being strangers. This principle calls for compassion and equitable treatment, even amidst complex policy...
reflection.zh: 关于国家边界和移民的辩论常常挑战社会，使其思考如何对待那些寻求入境的人。雅伟古老的命令提醒我们，要像对待本地人一样欢迎外国人，并回想我们自己作为陌生人的共同人类经历。这一原则呼唤着同情心和公平待遇，即使在复杂的政策讨论中也是如此。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Holdouts for Trump’s attorney general pick say they will advance his nomination to the full Senate – US politics live
title.zh: 特朗普司法部长人选称已与参议员达成协议，结束僵局——美国政治直播

summary.en: Todd Blanche, the attorney general pick, has reached an agreement with Republican senators to withdraw a $1.8 billion 'anti-weaponization fund'. This deal resolves a weeks-long standoff that had blocked his nomination.
summary.zh: 司法部长人选托德·布兰奇已与共和党参议员达成协议，撤回一项18亿美元的“反武器化基金”。这项协议解决了数周以来阻碍其提名的僵局。

body.en: Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis say that formal order withdrawing ‘anti-weaponization fund’ has addressed their concerns Blanche formally rescinds Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponization fund’ Sign up for the US Breaking News email On Tuesday, we’ll bring you the latest from Michigan where voters will head to the polls for competitive primaries in Senate and House races. The most closely watched competition is the Democratic primary for the US Senate, where congresswoman Haley Stevens is up against former public health official Abdul El-Sayed . They’re vying to ultimately win the seat of outgoing senator Gary Peters in November. The race has now turned into a proxy battle for the future of the Democratic party. Establishment-backed Stevens has received support from party leaders and her race has been buoyed by millions from the pro-Israel lobby. Meanwhile the insurgent El-Sayed has built a strong grassroots movement and is endorsed by progressives lawmakers in the Democratic caucus. Continue reading...
body.zh: 托德·布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 与阻碍其提名的共和党参议员进行了数周谈判后，正式下令撤回“反武器化基金” 布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 正式撤销特朗普 18 亿美元的“反武器化基金” 订阅美国突发新闻电子邮件 唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 今天将抵达华盛顿。他一天的大部分时间都在开会，但我们会在东部时间下午 1:30 收到他的消息，届时他将在椭圆形办公室签署行政命令。我们将为您带来最新的线路。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political standoffs often highlight the need for diverse perspectives in governance. The resolution of this nomination, achieved through weeks of negotiation and the withdrawal of a controversial fund, underscores the value of seeking counsel. It reminds us that collective wisdom can guide leaders toward decisions that serve the common good.
reflection.zh: 政治僵局常凸显治理中多元视角的必要性。这项提名通过数周的谈判和撤回一项有争议的基金而得以解决，强调了寻求忠告的价值。它提醒我们，集体的智慧可以引导领袖做出服务共同利益的决定。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: AstraZeneca shares plunge over talks with US cancer drug firm on $400bn merger
title.zh: 阿斯利康股价因与美国癌症药物公司4000亿美元合并谈判而暴跌

summary.en: AstraZeneca's shares fell sharply after reports emerged of its discussions to merge with US cancer drug firm Bristol Myers Squibb in a deal potentially worth $400 billion. Analysts have questioned the strategic rationale for the proposed tie-up, which would create the world's fourth-largest drugmaker.
summary.zh: 阿斯利康股价在有报道称其正与美国癌症药物公司百时美施贵宝进行价值可能高达4000亿美元的合并谈判后大幅下跌。分析师对这项拟议中的合并交易的战略理由提出质疑，该交易将缔造全球第四大制药商。

body.en: Bristol Myers Squibb tie-up would create world’s fourth largest drugmaker but analysts question rationale for deal More than £15bn was wiped off the value of Britain’s biggest drugmaker, AstraZeneca, on Monday after a report that it was in discussions to take over its US rival Bristol Myers Squibb in a deal that would create a near $400bn (£300bn) pharmaceutical group. AstraZeneca, run by Pascal Soriot, its longtime chief executive, is the second biggest listed company in the UK, with a market value of nearly £196bn before the news broke. BMS, headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey, and known for its cancer treatments, is worth $133bn. Continue reading...
body.zh: 百时美施贵宝 (Bristol Myers Squibb) 的合作将创建全球第四大制药商，但分析师质疑交易的理由周一，英国最大制药商阿斯利康 (AstraZeneca) 的市值蒸发了超过 150 亿英镑，此前有报道称，阿斯利康 (AstraZeneca) 正在讨论收购其美国竞争对手百时美施贵宝 (Bristol Myers Squibb)，该交易将创建一家价值近 4000 亿美元（约合 3000 亿英镑）的制药集团。阿斯利康 (AstraZeneca) 由长期担任首席执行官的帕斯卡·索里奥特 (Pascal Soriot) 运营，是英国第二大上市公司，消息传出前市值接近 1960 亿英镑。 BMS 总部位于新泽西州普林斯顿，以其癌症治疗而闻名，市值 1330 亿美元。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The ambition to create a global pharmaceutical giant through a $400 billion merger, only to see its rationale questioned and value plunge, reminds us of humanity's grand endeavors. Like the builders of Babel, we often strive for immense scale and power, yet Yahweh reminds us that true strength and lasting purpose come from Him, not from our own limitless...
reflection.zh: 斥资4000亿美元合并以打造全球制药巨头的雄心，却因其合理性受到质疑并导致价值暴跌，这提醒我们人类的宏伟事业。正如巴别塔的建造者一样，我们常常追求巨大的规模和权力，然而雅伟提醒我们，真正的力量和持久的目的是来自祂，而非我们自身无限的抱负。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Paris prosecutor investigates alleged bullying in government departments after suicide attempt
title.zh: 巴黎检察官调查政府部门涉嫌欺凌事件，此前有员工企图自杀

summary.en: The Paris state prosecutor has launched an inquiry into alleged workplace bullying within government departments, following two suicides and two attempted suicides among staff connected to the Prime Minister's office.
summary.zh: 巴黎检察官已对政府部门内涉嫌职场欺凌展开初步调查，此前有两名与总理办公室相关的部门员工自杀，另有两人企图自杀。

body.en: Internal inquiries also opened after two suicides and two attempted suicides of staff in departments connected to PM’s office The Paris state prosecutor has opened a preliminary inquiry into alleged workplace bullying after the attempted suicide of a staff member in a department connected to the French prime minister’s office, France Inter radio has revealed. The public radio station reported on Monday that two government workers in different departments had ended their lives in the past year, and two others had attempted suicide. The radio station said complaints of alleged workplace bullying had been made. Continue reading...
body.zh: 法国总理办公室相关部门的一名工作人员发生两起自杀事件和两起自杀未遂事件后，内部调查也已展开 法国国际广播电台透露，在法国总理办公室相关部门的一名工作人员发生自杀未遂事件后，巴黎国家检察官已对涉嫌工作场所欺凌行为展开初步调查。该公共广播电台周一报道称，去年，不同部门的两名政府工作人员结束了生命，另外两人试图自杀。该广播电台表示，已收到有关工作场所欺凌行为的投诉。继续阅读...

Even the prophet Elijah, overwhelmed by his burdens, once cried out to Yahweh, wishing for death. In such moments of deep anguish, we are reminded that Yahweh understands our suffering and offers a path towards healing and...
reflection.zh: 这则悲剧性的新闻提醒我们，有毒的工作环境会带来极度的绝望，将人推向崩溃的边缘。即使是先知以利亚，在重担之下也曾向雅伟呼求，求死。在如此深切的痛苦时刻，我们被提醒雅伟理解我们的苦难，并提供一条通向医治和复原的道路。

verse.textEn: He came to a broom bush, sat down under it and prayed that he might die. 'I have had enough, Yahweh,' he said. 'Take my life; I am no better than my ancestors.'
verse.textZh: 他自己在旷野走了一日的路程，来到一棵罗腾树下，就坐在那里求死，说：「雅伟啊，罢了！求你取我的性命，因为我不胜于我的列祖。」

title.en: Rhine falls to record low levels as drought strains Europe's rivers
title.zh: 由于干旱给欧洲河流带来压力，莱茵河水位降至历史最低水平

summary.en: Low water levels in the Rhine, Danube and Po have curtailed the transport of goods and reduced electricity output.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The River Rhine has fallen to record low levels in several locations in Germany and the Netherlands as prolonged heatwaves continue across Europe.

Last week, levels were measured in Cologne in western Germany and in Lobith, where the Rhine crosses from Germany into the Netherlands, that were lower than at any point since records began.

Other major European rivers with important transport, industrial and agricultural functions have also seen record low levels, including the Danube, which flows through 10 countries, and Italy's Po river.

Drought conditions remained stable and critical in most of Europe and worsened in central-western Europe in mid-July, according to the EU's Drought Observatories.

Renewed heatwave conditions are due to continue for at least another week, pushing temperatures above 40C in many central and southern European countries.

Germany's Low Water Information System (NIWIS) said that 44% of the Rhine measuring stations and 78% of those on the Danube had recorded extremely low water levels at the end of July.

The Rhine - which starts in the Swiss Alps and empties in the North Sea - is one of Europe's busiest waterways. Decreasing water levels have sparked concerns about the economic fallout of having to limit navigation and shipping.

On Friday, the navigable water depth at the chokepoint of Kaub near Koblenz hit the 2018 record low of 25cm, before recovering slightly on Monday.

The Kaub gauging station in western Germany is a key indicator of navigability on the Rhine because it measures how heavily cargo vessels can be loaded. Low water levels measured there can severely restrict inland shipping.

Martin Wolters of the Rhine Waterways and Shipping Authority told German outlet WDR that although shipping on the Rhine was unlikely to be suspended altogether, precautions would have to be taken, such as spreading out cargo among more vessels to make them less heavy.

In time, this can result in higher transport costs and supply bottlenecks, Wolters said.

"There comes a time when loads are too small to be worthwhile or vessel owners are worried about damaging their ships," one commodity trader told Reuters.

Last week, the waters of the Danube fell to the lowest levels for 30 years in several countries, including Serbia and Romania, forcing Hungary to shut down its only nuclear power plant.

"We don't know when we will be able to restart [the plant]," Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Monday. "We hope that it will happen as soon as possible and we hope that the cooling, liberating rain that the forecasters do not yet see coming will arrive."

The drought of the Danube is also causing serious disruption to power supplies in Serbia and Romania.

Serbia cut output at its coal-fired power plants due to the lack of water...
body.zh: 随着整个欧洲持续长时间的热浪，德国和荷兰的几个地方莱茵河水位已降至历史最低水平。 上周，德国西部科隆和莱茵河从德国流入荷兰的洛比斯测得的水位水平低于有记录以来的任何时候。 其他具有重要运输、工业和农业功能的欧洲主要河流也出现了创纪录的低水位，包括流经10个国家的多瑙河和意大利的波河。 据欧盟干旱观测站称，7 月中旬，欧洲大部分地区的干旱状况依然稳定且严峻，但中西欧地区的干旱状况更加恶化。 新一轮的热浪天气预计将持续至少一周，导致许多中欧和南欧国家的气温超过 40 摄氏度。 德国低水位信息系统（NIWIS）表示，7月底莱茵河上44%的测量站和多瑙河上78%的测量站记录到极低水位。 莱茵河发源于瑞士阿尔卑斯山，注入北海，是欧洲最繁忙的水道之一。水位下降引发了人们对必须限制航行和航运造成的经济影响的担忧。 周五，科布伦茨附近考布阻塞点的通航水深触及2018年历史最低点25厘米，周一略有回升。 德国西部的考布测量站是莱茵河适航性的关键指标，因为它测量货船的装载重量。那里测得的低水位会严重限制内陆航运。 莱茵河航道和航运管理局的马丁·沃尔特斯 (Martin Wolters) 告诉德国媒体 WDR，尽管莱茵河航运不太可能完全暂停，但必须采取预防措施，例如将货物分散到更多船只上，以减轻其重量。 沃尔特斯说，随着时间的推移，这可能会导致更高的运输成本和供应瓶颈。 一位大宗商品贸易商告诉路透社：“总有一天，装载量太小而不值得，或者船东担心损坏他们的船只。” 上周，包括塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚在内的多个国家多瑙河水位跌至30年来的最低水位，迫使匈牙利关闭其唯一的核电站。 “我们不知道什么时候能够重启[工厂]，”总理彼得·马扎尔周一表示。 “我们希望这会尽快发生，我们希望预报员还没有预见到的凉爽、令人放松的降雨将会到来。” 多瑙河的干旱还导致塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的电力供应严重中断。 由于缺水，塞尔维亚削减了燃煤电厂的产量......

reflection.en: This story draws attention to creation care and environmental responsibility. Genesis 2:15 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with faithful stewardship of creation, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到受造之物关怀与环保责任。Genesis 2:15提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以对受造之物的忠心管家来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.

title.en: Aung San Suu Kyi appears healthy in first confirmed outside contact for 2.5 years
title.zh: 昂山素季在两年半以来首次确认的外部接触中显得健康

summary.en: Myanmar's military government has released new photos showing detained leader Aung San Suu Kyi meeting with an official from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). This marks the first confirmed outside contact for Suu Kyi in two and a half years, and she reportedly appeared healthy.
summary.zh: 缅甸军政府发布了新照片，显示被拘禁的领导人昂山素季与红十字国际委员会（ICRC）的一名官员会面。这是昂山素季两年半以来首次获得确认的外部接触，据报道她看起来身体健康。

body.en:
Detained Burmese leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to meet a delegation from the International Committee of the Red Cross, the first confirmed outside contact with her since a letter to her son two and a half years ago.

In photographs of the meeting released by the military government Suu Kyi appeared to be healthy.

She was detained shortly after the armed forces deposed her government in 2021, and sentenced her to 33 years in jail on what are widely viewed as trumped-up charges, though her sentence has been reduced and she has been moved to house arrest .

Despite repeated assurances from the military that Suu Kyi is alive and well, they have never provided convincing evidence of this.

Her son Kim Aris has in recent months mounted an international campaign demanding proof of life for the 81-year-old democracy icon.

Now a delegation from the ICRC has been allowed to meet her – her first confirmed meeting with anyone outside the government for nearly four years.

Photographs released of her with the ICRC team led by its representative Arnaud de Baecque show Suu Kyi looking relaxed and well, although no details of her state of health have been given, nor of what they talked about.

"The visit was carried out in accordance with the ICRC's standards and procedures for visiting people deprived of liberty. This included the opportunity to speak with Daw Aung San Suu Kyi in private," the ICRC said in a short statement.

Kim Aris welcomed the news, saying the pictures appear real and his mother seemed to be in "good health".

"It takes quite a lot for me to say that because the military have spread a lot of disinformation and false news over the years, so I've learnt to ignore a large part of it, but on this occasion, I think we can believe what's been said," he told the BBC's Newshour programme.

The Myanmar government, still headed by coup leader Min Aung Hlaing and dominated by the military despite an election held earlier this year, is trying to end its diplomatic isolation in a series of official visits to neighbouring countries.

Among the top demands being made of Myanmar's military leadership is that they end the aerial bombardment of opposition-held areas, start negotiations to end the civil war, and release Aung San Suu Kyi.

They have so far rejected those calls, but the publication of this morning's meeting suggests they may be willing to accede to the last demand.

title.en: Iran says it is in talks with Oman but not the US after Trump says negotiations to resume
title.zh: 特朗普建议周一与伊朗重启谈判

summary.en: President Trump has proposed new talks with Iran to begin on Monday, though Tehran has not yet responded to the suggestion. This comes after previous claims by Trump that a negotiated end to the conflict was near, only for military strikes to resume.
summary.zh: 特朗普总统提议周一与伊朗重启谈判，但德黑兰尚未对此建议作出回应。此前，特朗普曾表示冲突的谈判解决已近在咫尺，但随后军事打击又重新开始。

body.en:
Iran says it is negotiating with Oman to reach "an understanding" over a temporary route through the Strait of Hormuz to allow commercial shipping to resume.

The statement came after US President Donald Trump said new talks on ending the war in Iran would begin on Monday - and that he had called off "massive" strikes on the country for this purpose.

Trump did not specify who would take part in the talks. Earlier he had said the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed - and would include reopening Hormuz, the vital waterway whose closure by Iran has sent oil prices soaring.

In its response, Iran said it was not negotiating with the US - and had no plans to do so.

Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei added that Tehran was negotiating with Oman to reach "an understanding over a path to ensure the security of shipping passage through the Strait of Hormuz".

Tehran has repeatedly closed off the strait since the US and Israel started attacks on the country in February.

Talks to end the conflict - mostly facilitated by mediators - collapsed last month, ending a ceasefire agreed in April.

Trump has repeatedly vowed that a negotiated end to the war is near, only for tit-for-tat strikes to resume.

Speaking on board Air Force One on Sunday, he said Iran "knew the extent" of the planned US strikes "because they saw it forming", adding: "We're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon."

Trump declined to outline a deadline for a deal to be struck with Tehran, adding: "We'll just see how it is. We're ready to go anytime we want... I'm not looking to kill people."

Trump added that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman - as well as US partners such as the United Arab Emirates and Qatar - had urged him against conducting strikes over the weekend.

"We were all set to go," Trump said. "The reason they asked is [that] they think there's a deal," he said. "There's a deal on Hormuz, and there will be a deal on the nuclear."

Global oil prices fell on Monday morning in Asia trading after Trump's announcement. Brent Crude oil was down by 4.5% at $83.98 (£62.26), while US-traded oil was 4.6% lower at $80.74 (£59.85).

Energy prices have fluctuated since the conflict started on 28 February as traders reacted to disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Around 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) usually flows through the strait.

Vessel-tracking data from trade intelligence company Kpler suggests commercial shipping through the strait has slowed.

According to the data, 51 vessel crossings occurred through the strait between 30 July and 2 August. This is a drop of around 28% compared to the previous 4 days, in which 71 crossings were recorded through the strait.

title.en: Can PM Modi reconnect with India's Gen Z?
title.zh: 莫迪总理能否与印度 Z 世代重新建立联系？

summary.en: Student protests exposed a growing disconnect between PM Narendra Modi's BJP and young Indians. Experts say Instagram reels alone won't close it.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Student protests exposed a growing disconnect between PM Narendra Modi's BJP and young Indians. Experts say Instagram reels alone won't close it.

As students filled India's streets to demand accountability from the government , Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi seemed to have realized that he needed to connect more effectively with the country's youth.

Modi posted on Instagram a rare selfie video in which he said he was pained by their suffering and promised remedial steps. But it was not enough to satisfy the protesters' concerns, and five Gen Z-style reels later, that gap seems as wide as ever.

"We ain't friends," one comment under the first reel read. It echoed thousands of others reacting to a midnight video drop from the PM. 

In one of Modi's lesser-produced videos, he addressed the youth as "friends" before finally speaking about the exam at the center of the protests.

It was the prime minister’s response to the biggest political crisis he has faced in his third term so far, over a cancelled high-stakes medical entrance exam which affected millions of aspirants.

Since the first video, he's improved camera angles and lighting, tried varied backgrounds, and even started and ended the videos himself like a one-man content creator. The response remains tepid.

For Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the protests came at the peak of its power, but the unrest has dimmed that shine, and the disconnect with the youth is substantial, experts told DW.

In 2024, the average age of MPs elected to India's Parliament reached a record 56 years, which is a problem, said Shipra Baduni, CEO of Young Leaders for Active Citizenship, because there is not much youth representation in the legislature. 

India has traditionally had vibrant youth participation at the university level, where student parties have long been affiliated with national and regional parties. 

"Student politics has not only given a pulse check, or given a platform for young people to be able to express frustration, or anger, or dissent," said Baduni. "It's also given some of these parties and leaders today."

"We've seen systematically over the last one decade that it has been cut down," she added. "There is a very evident push to say that students should only study, and there is no need for students to engage in politics."

"Where is the space for a young person to express their frustration? If you go on social media to criticize the government, there is a crackdown. Offices are screening your social media."

title.en: Moroccan king's letter confirms naming of major highway in honour of Trump
title.zh: 摩洛哥国王的信确认以特朗普的名义命名主要高速公路

summary.en: The highway enters Western Sahara, a disputed territory that Morocco claims sovereignty over.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A letter from Morocco's King Mohammed VI has confirmed that the country has named a major highway after US President Donald Trump.

Last week, in a social media post, Trump thanked the king for the honour, but there was not a parallel announcement from the Moroccan authorities.

But Morocco's state press agency has published a letter the king wrote to the president telling him that the name-change was taking place as "a personal expression of my high regard".

Formerly the Tiznit-Dakhla highway, the road enters Western Sahara, most of which Morocco occupies and claims sovereignty over. But part is controlled by the Polisario Front, an armed group seeking independence for the local Sahrawi people.

In 2020, during the first Trump administration, the US recognised Morocco's claim over the disputed region as part of a deal whereby Morocco agreed to normalise relations with Israel.

In his letter, dated 2 July but published over the weekend, King Mohammed highlighted what he called the US president's "historic recognition... of Morocco's sovereignty over its Sahara" saying that it would "forever be etched in the memory of Moroccans, from generation to generation".

"Although our relations have always been rooted in close friendship and constant loyalty, they have never been as vigorous and fruitful as during your two presidential terms," the king added.

The monarch called the 1,055km (655 mile) highway a "strategic axis" linking "north and south of Morocco". Morocco calls Western Sahara its "southern provinces".

A former Spanish colony, Western Sahara - which is considered a "non-self-governing territory" by the UN - has been fought over for five decades in one of Africa's longest conflicts.

The UN has consistently pushed for a solution to the dispute, including a referendum, but the indigenous people of the area have never been able to vote for their own future.

European governments have until recently avoided taking sides. But some, including the UK and Spain have backed Morocco's plan to grant Western Sahara autonomy but deny it independence.

Trump's Truth Social post on the renaming last week also included a video about the road saying that it cost nearly $1bn (£740m) to build.

"I look forward to traveling the entire length of this great highway someday, hopefully soon!" the president wrote.

Morocco wants tourists to visit Western Sahara. Some say it's tightening its control

title.en: Russia: Bridge-building with North Korea
title.zh: 俄罗斯：与朝鲜架起桥梁

summary.en: In the far east, well away from world events, Russia and North Korea are building their first road connection. The project has set alarm bells ringing in Ukraine.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In the far east, well away from world events, Russia and North Korea are building their first road connection. The project has set alarm bells ringing in Ukraine.

For years, Khasan was little more than a very remote place on the edge of Russia . Less than 500 people live in the village in the country's far east, more than 5,600 miles (9,012 kilometers) from Moscow. But it's here that Russia shares a mere 10.5-mile border with North Korea — and Khasan is the only Russian settlement along that short stretch. Since 1959, the so-called Korean-Russian Friendship Railway Bridge has crossed the Tumen River here, serving as the only land connection between the two countries.

But in recent years, Russia and North Korea have been building a parallel road bridge just a few hundred yards away. The bridge is now nearing completion ahead of schedule, raising concerns in Kyiv that Russia could use it to secretly bring North Korean troops to the front lines in Ukraine .

Since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Moscow and Pyongyang have improved their ties . Both countries face Western sanctions and are diplomatically largely isolated. In June 2024, Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a strategic partnership deal which in part focused on expanding military cooperation. That meant large-scale weapons shipments as well as the deployment of North Korean soldiers to support Russia's war in Ukraine. At the same time, both governments agreed to build the new road bridge.

"The opening of the new bridge will boost bilateral trade, optimize logistics, strengthen cultural ties and transform border regions into dynamically growing economic centers," Russian Transport Minister Andrey Nikitin said at the time.

The Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) has also pointed to the bridge's economic significance, noting that "the pace at which construction of the road bridge is progressing, and the continued high level of rail traffic at previously dormant rail yards, are clear indicators of the importance and expansion of trade between the two countries during Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine."

But according to  British newspaper  The Guardian , there are major doubts that civilian economic goals are the project's true primary purpose.

Official data shows that trade between Russia and North Korea amounted to just $34 million in 2024. The bridge and its immediate infrastructure are thought to cost roughly $100 million. Satellite pictures of the site show warehouses, customs facilities, truck areas and a helicopter pad being built.

title.en: As Australia is hit with mass mortalities, here’s how NZ has prepared for bird flu
title.zh: 澳大利亚遭遇大规模死亡，新西兰如何为禽流感做准备

summary.en: Australia is experiencing significant wildlife deaths due to bird flu. Its neighbor, New Zealand, has spent years researching how the lethal virus could affect its unique animal populations and preparing for such an event.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚正遭受禽流感导致的野生动物大规模死亡。其邻国新西兰已花费数年时间研究这种致命病毒将如何影响其独特的野生动物，并为此类事件做好了准备。

body.en:
When a swamp harrier hawk — known also as a kāhu — was found tangled in a fence in a thinly populated part of New Zealand's North Island in early July, no one thought much about the discovery.

But when the battered scavenger was put down the following day after its health deteriorated, a routine test would enshrine the bird in history.

It was the first native New Zealand bird to test positive for the highly virulent, often lethal strain of H5N1 bird flu which had been detected on Australia's mainland for the first time just a month prior.

"There's lots of birds that go between Australia and New Zealand; although there is a sea between us, we're way more connected than we might like to think," says Jemma Geoghegan from the University of Otago.

A month on, the virus is slowly making its way into the region's eco-systems. New Zealand has recorded two cases of the virus but officials there expect that number to start climbing steeply any day now.

Australia, meanwhile, has just recorded its first mass casualty event: 49 dead greater crested terns and 35 sick ones were discovered on rocks off Cape Jaffa, an isolated outcrop on South Australia's rugged limestone coast.

Both countries knew the virus was not far off when it was first detected on Australia's remote sub-Antarctic Heard Island in 2025, leading to mass mortality of elephant seals.

By this time, preparations for the strain — which has ripped through every other continent — were well underway in New Zealand, where for the past two years the country's Department of Conservation has been trialling a vaccination program for six species of "highly" endangered birds.

Two years ago the country began researching how certain native birds would tolerate and respond to the vaccine, so when the disease made its inevitable landfall, these populations could be protected.

"The trial was really to understand if the vaccine was going to be effective, but also what kind of doses different birds might need."

She said this "targeted program" had been rolled out for species that were "really, really endangered" and already "highly managed" through GPS trackers and health monitoring.

The vaccine being used in New Zealand requires a booster shot to be effective, so it's important that researchers are able to carefully track which birds have had the jab and which haven't.

"Often they'll be on offshore islands that are highly managed, because there's only maybe a few 100 left of the individuals."

title.en: Cuba suffers yet another nationwide blackout
title.zh: 古巴再次遭遇全国性停电

summary.en: Cuba has experienced another nationwide power outage, the fourth since July, as its electricity grid continues to struggle under a US-imposed oil blockade.
summary.zh: 古巴再次遭遇全国性停电，这是继七月以来第四次，该国电网在美国实施的石油禁运下持续面临困境。

body.en:
Cuba's electricity grid has collapsed again after three nationwide blackouts in July. The power failure comes amid a US-imposed oil blockade on the communist island.

  Cuba 's state-owned grid operator said the island's power system collapsed late on Sunday, the latest in a series of rolling power cuts caused by aging infrastructure and a US energy embargo .

The state-run utility UNE said there was a "total disconnection" of the national electricity system, which means the entire country of 10 million people, including the capital, Havana, has been plunged into darkness.

The Ministry of Energy said that protocols to reactivate the grid were underway.

The series of outages afflicting the island in recent times have also affected water supplies and cooling systems, making normal life extremely difficult.

Cuba, which relies largely on aging oil-fired power plants, lost access to fuel from its previous primary supplier, Venezuela, after US President Donald Trump imposed an oil blockade following Washington's ouster and capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on January 3 .  

Imports from Mexico , which subsequently became Cuba's key supplier of oil, have also ceased under US pressure.

Supplies brought by a single Russian tanker in March with Washington's authorization have been exhausted.

Cuba is also facing other pressure from the US, including ramped-up sanctions against Cuban state-owned businesses imposed by the Trump administration.

These have led to a number of foreign companies suspending their operations in the island.

Washington has also indicted former President Raul Castro over the downing of two civilian planes 30 years ago, in which three US citizens and a US resident died. 

The US redesignated the communist island as a "state sponsor of terrorism" for a third time in 2025, shortly after former President Joe Biden moved to have it deleted from the list.

title.en: 'Deeply saddened': Australian helicopter provider speaks after Greece firefighting tragedy
title.zh: “深感悲痛”：希腊消防悲剧后，澳大利亚直升机供应商发声

summary.en: McDermott Aviation, an Australian helicopter provider, has expressed profound sadness following a firefighting tragedy in Greece, where helicopters leased by the company were involved as wildfires continue to spread across southern Europe.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚直升机供应商麦克德莫特航空对希腊消防悲剧表示深切哀悼，该公司租赁的直升机参与了扑灭南欧持续蔓延的野火。

body.en:
Two crew members have died after two helicopters — leased by Australian company McDermott Aviation — collided midair while battling wildfires in Greece on Sunday.

A Greek and a Danish national were killed in the crash over Psatha, an area west of Athens, according to Greece's fire service. Two crew members from Greece and Britain who were operating a separate helicopter were found alive.

Founder and president of McDermott Aviation, John McDermott said he was "deeply saddened" by news of the fatal collision.

"We are deeply saddened to confirm that the two crew members aboard one of the helicopters have lost their lives. The two crew members from the second helicopter are in the care of medical professionals.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident. Both crews were undertaking the critical work of supporting firefighting operations to help protect communities."

McDermott Aviation has reportedly operated in Greece for several years. The company said it is working closely with relevant authorities as they undertake an investigation into the cause of the incident.

Over the past decade, McDermott Aviation said it has engaged in around 10 to 12 international movements a year via sea and air freight. It also operates in New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the United States, which is currently experiencing wildfires in several western states.

Nikos Pagiotelis has been a volunteer firefighter in Greece for more than 20 years. He told SBS Greek about the moment he heard news of the crash over local radio.

"When you are inside the fire, and you are trying to help the people, you're trying to save the animals, save the forest. Then suddenly [you] hear that two helicopters have crashed a couple of miles near you — you can understand that something really hurts inside," Pagiotelis said.

"You can do nothing, you freeze for a little bit, and then you just continue your work. You continue to help people to honour the lives of the loss of two comrades."

In a statement on social media, Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also expressed his "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the deceased firefighters.

"The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot at the time they were attempting the major fire in Porto Gremeno fills us all with grief," Mitsotakis said.

Nearly 500 firefighters and 23 aircraft have been deployed to fight fires in Greece, which have been driven by high temperatures and gale-force winds.

title.en: Man arrested over death of British woman found in suitcase in Athens
title.zh: 男子因雅典行李箱女尸案被捕

summary.en: A man has been arrested in connection with the death of Elisabeth-Jane Ross, a Scottish national whose body was found last month in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens.
summary.zh: 一名男子因涉嫌苏格兰公民伊丽莎白-简·罗斯的死亡而被捕。她的尸体上个月在雅典一栋废弃建筑的行李箱中被发现。

body.en:
The body of Scottish national Elisabeth-Jane Ross was discovered last month in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens.

A 26-year-old man has been arrested by Greek police in connection with the death of a British woman whose body was found in a suitcase in Athens last month.

"Officers of the Directorate for Combating Organized Crime have solved the homicide of a 38-year-old UK national, whose body was found inside a suitcase in an abandoned building in the Kypseli area on July 18," the Hellenic Police said on Sunday.

The victim, identified in British and Greek media reports as 38-year-old Elisabeth-Jane Ross from Scotland, arrived in Greece in late June and was last known to be in the Athens area on July 10. She was later reported missing.

Police said the suspect, a foreign national, confessed on Thursday and now faces charges including intentional homicide, robbery and firearms-related offenses.

"It emerged that the [suspect] placed the body in a suitcase and transported it to the abandoned premises. Furthermore, in the days that followed, the 26-year-old used the victim's bank cards to withdraw sums of money," police said.

According to reports, the suspect said the victim was already dead when he found her, although police made no mention of this in their statement.

Greek police said international cooperation, including support from Interpol authorities in the US and UK law enforcement agencies, helped identify the victim despite advanced decomposition.

title.en: Israel kills 18 in Gaza despite Trump's announcement of Hamas disarmament deal
title.zh: 以色列袭击加沙致18人死亡，部长称无协议停止攻击

summary.en: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza have resulted in 18 deaths, continuing despite a US announcement of a potential path for Hamas' disarmament. A minister stated there is no agreement to halt the attacks.
summary.zh: 尽管美国宣布了哈马斯解除武装的途径，以色列对加沙的空袭仍在继续，造成18人死亡。一位部长表示，目前没有停止袭击的协议。

body.en:
Israeli airstrikes hit Gaza for a second straight day on Monday, killing at least 18 Palestinians, medics said, despite US President Donald Trump's announcement of a breakthrough in efforts to implement last year's ceasefire agreement.

From dawn, Israeli warplanes hit Gaza City in the north, the central city of Deir al-Balah and the southern area of Khan Younis, causing the biggest daily death toll in weeks, according to Palestinian health officials.

Trump's assertion on Friday that Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups had agreed to disarm had raised hopes of a turning point in efforts to end the conflict.

On Sunday, Israeli energy minister Eli Cohen — a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet — said the government would give Hamas the opportunity to disarm but that he was "very sceptical" that would happen.

Cohen told Israel's Army Radio there had been no deal to halt attacks on Gaza and that he saw a need for Israel, which already occupies 70 per cent of the enclave, to take full control of it if Hamas did not disarm.

"In the deal we signed with the United States, our stance is that Hamas must be dismantled. This is the first thing that must happen," he added.

Later on Sunday, a spokesperson for Netanyahu's office told Reuters news agency that Israel expressed concerns to the US on the disarmament plan.

"The most important concern for Israel is that nothing can happen before Hamas completely and truly disarms ...," Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli prime minister's office, said.

Strikes on Deir al-Balah killed at least four people, Palestinian health officials said, and a separate attack wounded five people and set some tents ablaze in Mawasi, near Khan Younis, according to the civil emergency service.

A couple and their nine-year-old son were killed in a strike on a house in Mawasi, Palestinian officials said.

Another couple was killed with their child in a strike on an apartment in Gaza City, where two more people died in a strike on a tent near the office of the Egyptian representative mission, medics said. Later on Sunday, another two people were killed in the city's eastern Zeitoun neighbourhood, they added.

One person was killed near Jabalia in northern Gaza, Palestinian officials said.

In a subsequent attack on Gaza City, medics said an Israeli airstrike on a car killed at least three Palestinians near Saraya Square.

Trump's Board of Peace, the US-led body overseeing the ceasefire, published on Friday a 15-point roadmap setting out the final steps for implementing the agreement .

title.en: Trump says fresh Iran talks set to begin after major strikes called off
title.zh: 特朗普称取消重大打击后，新的伊朗谈判即将开始

summary.en: Former President Trump announced that new talks with Iran are expected to commence after planned military strikes were called off. Mediators are working to restore a June memorandum of understanding, though the path to a lasting peace agreement remains challenging.
summary.zh: 前总统特朗普宣布，在取消了原定的军事打击后，与伊朗的新一轮谈判即将开始。尽管和平之路依然充满挑战，伊朗调解员仍在努力恢复六月份的谅解备忘录。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump says new negotiations with Iran will begin on Monday, after he decided to hold off on striking the Islamic republic to pursue a deal to end the war that's now entering its sixth month.

Trump told reporters on Monday that the talks would cover the Strait of Hormuz — a route for global energy supplies that has become a key sticking point in the conflict — and ultimately, the de-nuclearisation of Iran.

For its part, Iran said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the strait, where a tanker reported an explosion nearby on Monday, underscoring the continued volatility of the strategic waterway.

The US and Iran have been at war since 28 February, when the US and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, though months of on-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.

Following a return to strikes last month, fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again. Trump had threatened to hit Iran "very hard" and was reportedly considering renewed attacks, including against energy infrastructure, with US embassies across the region on alert.

Trump pulled back from that threat Saturday, saying the "perimeters" of a deal were there.

"Now what we're doing is we're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon," Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday, without providing details of the venue or participants in the talks.

The US president said he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on the strikes, which he claimed would have been "the biggest attack since World War II".

A previous ceasefire deal that included the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz fell through, and Iran has since tightened its control over the waterway.

The US president said at the start of the conflict that the war was necessary to deal with Iran's nuclear program. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Iran insists the program is entirely civilian in nature.

Iranian politician Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesman for the parliament's national security commission, said on Sunday that mediators were trying to revive the so-called Islamabad memorandum of understanding, which was agreed in June.

That memorandum was not intended as a final peace deal, but as a stepping stone to negotiations on a comprehensive agreement, though it did include provisions on Hormuz.

"They know that the main issue and, in fact, the key to the matter right now is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz, so yes, there is an exchange of views," Ghashghavi said.

title.en: China: Dozens dead in Gansu flash floods
title.zh: 中国：甘肃山洪致数十人死亡

summary.en: Chinese authorities will launch an investigation into the floods, amid warnings of further landslides as the rainy weather continues, after dozens were killed in Gansu province.

body.en:
Chinese authorities will launch an investigation into the floods, amid warnings of further landslides as the rainy weather continues.

The death toll after a flash flood in the northern Gansu province of  China has climbed to 25, according to state media reports.

The flood has left 23 others injured, the ⁠official Xinhua news agency reported on Sunday.

The Shuangshimen Scenic Area, a popular tourist spot for camping, was hit by a flash flood on July 26, with state media initially reporting 10 deaths and 23 injuries.

The country's national commission for disaster prevention said it would oversee an investigation into the event.

Videos of the flood show a deluge ripping through a valley where several tents and cars were parked.

Authorities have warned of further landslides, including in ‌Dingxi, ​as heavy downpour continues in the annual flood season.

Beijing and Inner Mongolia also issued weather warnings on Sunday as China's ​weather observatory warned of heavy rain, high winds and thunderstorms across a large stretch of the country from ⁠the southwest ​to the northeast.

reflection.en: The tragic flash floods in Gansu, claiming dozens of lives and threatening further landslides, remind us of the profound vulnerability of creation. Yahweh's word tells us that the whole creation groans under the weight of brokenness, a reality keenly felt in the wake of such natural disasters. In these moments of loss and uncertainty, we are called to...
reflection.zh: 甘肃省发生的悲惨山洪夺走了数十人的生命，并预警可能发生更多山体滑坡，这提醒我们受造界的脆弱。雅伟的话语告诉我们，整个受造界都在破碎的重压下呻吟，这种现实在自然灾害发生后感受尤为深刻。在这些失落和不确定的时刻，我们被呼召去怜悯，并盼望万物的最终更新。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: China has banned hidden retractable car door handles. How are they dangerous – and what will Australia do?
title.zh: 中国已禁止隐藏式可伸缩汽车门把手。它们为何危险？澳大利亚会效仿吗？

summary.en: China has banned hidden retractable car door handles, citing their failure to operate during accidents and trapping passengers in burning vehicles. These handles were popularized by Tesla electric vehicles, and the move raises questions about whether other countries like Australia will follow suit.
summary.zh: 中国已禁止使用隐藏式可伸缩汽车门把手，理由是它们在事故中可能失灵，导致乘客被困在燃烧的车辆中。特斯拉电动汽车普及了这种门把手，此举引发了其他国家（如澳大利亚）是否会效仿的疑问。

body.en: The handles, which were popularised by Elon Musk’s Tesla EVs, have a record of failing and trapping passengers inside burning vehicles during deadly accidents Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast They used to be a novelty in Australia: the futuristic, flush-mounted car door handles favoured by Elon Musk’s Tesla. However while the design – popularised with the Tesla Model S in 2012 and since adopted by other manufacturers – might look sleek, it may not be great in an emergency. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这些把手因埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的特斯拉电动汽车而广受欢迎，但在致命事故中曾发生过故障，并将乘客困在燃烧的车辆内。 关注我们的澳大利亚新闻直播博客，了解最新动态 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 它们曾经是澳大利亚的新奇事物：埃隆·马斯克 (Telsas) 青睐的未来派嵌入式汽车门把手。然而，虽然这种设计在 2012 年随特斯拉 Model S 流行起来，后来被其他制造商采用，但虽然看起来很时尚，但在紧急情况下可能不太好。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The ban on retractable car door handles highlights the importance of foresight in design and technology. A prudent person foresees danger and takes precautions, reminding us that innovation must always be balanced with safety and the well-being of others. This decision underscores the responsibility to protect lives by addressing foreseeable risks, even in...
reflection.zh: 对可伸缩汽车门把手的禁令突显了设计和技术中预见危险的重要性。通达人预见祸患就藏躲，提醒我们创新必须始终与安全和他人福祉相平衡。这一决定强调了通过解决可预见的风险来保护生命的责任，即使是在看似微小的设计选择中。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: China’s tech advances are causing chaos from Silicon Valley to the White House
title.zh: 中国的科技进步正在从硅谷到白宫引发混乱

summary.en: Recent advancements in China's artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing, and robotics technologies have caused significant disruption in global financial markets and the US tech industry.
summary.zh: 中国在人工智能、芯片制造和机器人技术方面取得的最新进展，已在全球金融市场和美国科技行业引发了显著的震荡。

body.en: New AI models, advanced robots and specialty computer chips are unsettling markets and the US tech industry Over the past month, a series of advancements in China’s artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing and robotics technologies have rattled financial markets, caused divisions among US tech moguls and left the Trump administration scrambling to respond. Silicon Valley has long pointed to China’s tech industry as a competitive threat and used its growth as rationale for why US firms should not face regulatory oversight that could slow them down. In recent weeks, however, China’s progress has pushed US tech CEOs past vague warnings and into open disagreement over how to address Chinese-made products upending their industry. Continue reading...
body.zh: 新的人工智能模型、先进机器人和专用计算机芯片令市场和美国科技行业感到不安。过去一个月，中国人工智能、芯片制造和机器人技术的一系列进步震惊了金融市场，引发了美国科技大亨之间的分歧，并让特朗普政府仓促应对。硅谷长期以来一直将中国科技行业视为竞争威胁，并以中国科技行业的增长作为美国企业不应面临可能放慢发展速度的监管监督的理由。然而，最近几周，中国的进步让美国科技公司的首席执行官不再发出含糊的警告，而是在如何解决颠覆其行业的中国制造产品问题上产生了公开分歧。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid pace of technological innovation, particularly in AI and robotics, reflects a time when knowledge is indeed increasing at an unprecedented rate. This acceleration can bring both wonder and apprehension as societies grapple with its profound implications. In such moments, we are reminded to seek wisdom beyond mere information, trusting Yahweh to...
reflection.zh: 人工智能和机器人技术等领域的快速创新步伐，正反映出知识以前所未有的速度增长的时代。这种加速既带来惊奇，也引发担忧，因为社会正在努力应对其深远影响。在这样的时刻，我们被提醒要寻求超越单纯信息的智慧，信靠雅伟引导我们穿越新的领域。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: World-renowned climber Nirmal Purja among 11 struck by avalanche on Pakistan mountain
title.zh: 世界著名登山家尼尔马尔·普尔贾等11人在巴基斯坦山脉遭遇雪崩

summary.en: World-renowned climber Nirmal Purja was among 11 mountaineers caught in a deadly avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan. Rescuers have found four bodies as the search continues for the team.
summary.zh: 世界著名登山家尼尔马尔·普尔贾是11名在巴基斯坦布洛阿特峰遭遇致命雪崩的登山者之一。救援人员已找到四具遗体，搜寻工作仍在进行中。

body.en: Rescuers say four bodies found in search for team caught in Broad Peak avalanche, after trackers showed rapid descent The world-renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja – a former British special forces member – is among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak. The Alpine Club of Pakistan said “seven climbers have been spotted via aerial drone footage” adding that “their identities and condition cannot yet be verified”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 救援人员称，在追踪器显示快速下降后，在寻找布洛阿特峰雪崩中陷入雪崩的登山队时，发现了四具尸体。世界著名的尼泊尔登山家尼尔马尔·普贾（Nirmal Purja）是一名前英国特种部队成员，他是巴基斯坦布洛阿特峰遭遇雪崩的 11 名登山者之一。巴基斯坦高山俱乐部表示，“通过无人机航拍发现了七名登山者”，并补充说“他们的身份和状况尚未得到证实”。继续阅读...

reflection.zh: 登山者遭遇雪崩的悲剧性新闻提醒我们生命的脆弱和失去的突然。在极度悲伤和痛苦的时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟有一天将擦去我们所有眼泪的应许。这个盼望向我们保证，苦难、哀伤和死亡终将过去。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

body.zh: 从中华帝国到当今的印度，学生运动不断地采用他们那个时代的工具和符号来挑战权威。 2026 年 7 月 22 日，在多雨的印度孟买，一名穿着休闲的年轻女子走到一辆载着被拘留学生的缓慢行驶的警车前。她将手掌放在引擎盖上，迫使车辆停了下来。 手机从各个角度捕捉了这一时刻。她也举起了自己的手机，记录了这次遭遇。几个小时内，这段视频就传遍了印度及其他地区。 它成为蟑螂简塔党抗议活动的标志性视觉效果之一，在印度医学入学考试泄密后，学生们在这场运动中要求透明度和问责制。 但这一刻的​​力量不仅在于她所做的事情，还在于她的所作所为很快被人们看到。一个年轻女子对抗权威的一个动作，成为了数百万屏幕上共享的符号。 虽然这段视频属于在社交媒体上长大的一代人，但其背后的冲动却要古老得多。 从法庭请愿书和革命海报到照片、雨伞和模因，学生运动不断地调整他们可用的工具和符号，将它们变成异议的工具。 早在电视或社交媒体跨境传播异议之前，学生们就已经找到了表达不满的方法。 例如，在中国东汉，太学的学者与具有改革思想的官员结盟，反对宫廷中有权有势的宦官，许多人认为宦官腐败且在政治上专横。 他们通过公开批评、政治网络和请愿来表达他们的反对意见。 在政治沟通通过官方渠道进行的时代，请愿是向王室表达不满的既定方式之一。它们以正式语言编写并通过官僚机构传达，将学生的担忧直接传达到国家的沟通系统中。 1968 年的巴黎，学生们挑战大学当局和保守的战后社会秩序。随着示威活动在法国首都蔓延并吸引了工人，该运动最持久的贡献之一来自巴黎美术学院的一个地下室工作室。 Atelier Populaire（“人民工作室”）在抗议期间印制了数千张海报，其中许多是在一夜之间印制的。他们大胆的图形、轮廓和口号成为了这场运动的视觉语言。许多作品都是集体制作的，没有作者的名字，这有助于将抗议转变为公众的共同声音。 这些海报及其信息可能会在一夜之间出现在数十个地方，使抗议活动在当地得到广泛的关注。 当图像可以跨境传输时，抗议的影响力也变得更大。 在...

reflection.en: Student movements, by making their dissent visible, often echo a deep human longing for fairness and moral order. Yahweh, through the prophet Amos, calls for justice to flow powerfully and consistently, reminding us that true righteousness should be an undeniable force in society. This pursuit of a more just world often requires courage to speak truth to...
reflection.zh: 学生运动通过使异议显现，常常回应着人类对公平和道德秩序的深切渴望。雅伟通过先知阿摩司呼吁，愿公平如大水滚滚，使公义如江河滔滔，提醒我们真正的公义应成为社会中不可否认的力量。这种对更公正世界的追求，往往需要勇气向权力说出真相，即使这意味着挑战现状。

verse.textEn: Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!
verse.textZh: 惟愿公平如大水滚滚，使公义如江河滔滔。

title.en: Chinese super-embassy in London to go ahead after high court challenge dismissed
title.zh: 中国驻伦敦超级大使馆在高院驳回挑战后将继续建设

summary.en: A high court in London has dismissed a challenge from local residents against the construction of a new Chinese embassy. The residents' association, which sought to stop planning permission, has announced its intention to appeal the ruling.
summary.zh: 伦敦高等法院驳回了当地居民对中国新大使馆建设的挑战。寻求阻止规划许可的居民协会表示将对该裁决提出上诉。

body.en: Royal Mint Court residents’ association, which sought to stop planning permission, says it will appeal against ruling Construction of a controversial new Chinese embassy was given the green light on Friday after the high court dismissed a challenge from neighbours. The Royal Mint Court residents’ association (RMCRA), which brought the case against the government, immediately announced plans to appeal against the decision, in a move that could cause further delays to the project. The debate over planning permission for the new embassy has been a sore point of British-Chinese relations in recent years. Continue reading...
body.zh: 寻求停止规划许可的皇家造币厂居民协会表示，在高等法院驳回邻国的质疑后，周五，有争议的中国新大使馆建设项目获得批准，该协会表示将对裁决提出上诉。对政府提起诉讼的皇家造币厂居民协会 (RMCRA) 立即宣布计划对该决定提出上诉，此举可能会导致该项目进一步延误。关于新使馆规划许可的争论一直是近年来英中关系的一个痛点。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Even amidst legal disputes and community tensions, the call to live peaceably with all people remains a guiding principle. While residents pursue their appeal, this situation reminds us of the ongoing effort required to foster good relationships, even between powerful entities and their neighbors. Yahweh desires that we strive for harmony wherever possible.
reflection.zh: 即使在法律纠纷和社区紧张局势中，与所有人和平相处的呼吁仍然是一个指导原则。当居民们继续上诉时，这种情况提醒我们，即使是强大的实体与邻里之间，也需要持续努力培养良好关系。雅伟希望我们尽可能地追求和谐。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Could AI take your job? Some workers in China already know the answer
title.zh: 人工智能会取代你的工作吗？中国一些工人已经知道了答案

summary.en: Workers across China are expressing concern about the potential impact of artificial intelligence on their jobs and livelihoods, amidst an already unstable labor market.
summary.zh: 在中国各地，工人们对人工智能在日益脆弱的劳动力市场中对其生计的影响感到担忧。

body.en: Across the country, workers are fearful about the impact of AI on their livelihoods in an increasingly fragile labour market On the tree-lined streets of Wuhan, where cars jostle for space with mopeds and cargo trucks, the malfunctioning of a new type of vehicle has recently been causing chaos on the city’s roads. In March, several cars from a fleet of driverless taxis stopped abruptly in the streets. The “system malfunction” left distressed riders stranded for hours. The robotaxis, known as Apollo Go and powered by artificial intelligence (AI), were taken off Wuhan’s streets for months for investigations. Continue reading...
body.zh: 在日益脆弱的劳动力市场中，全国各地的工人们都担心人工智能会对他们的生计产生影响。在武汉绿树成荫的街道上，汽车与轻便摩托车和货运卡车争夺空间，最近一种新型车辆的故障导致该市道路出现混乱。三月份，无人驾驶出租车车队中的几辆车突然停在街上。 “系统故障”让心疼的乘客滞留了几个小时。这辆名为 Apollo Go 的机器人出租车由人工智能 (AI) 驱动，已被带离武汉街道数月以进行调查。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As technological advancements like AI reshape the world of work, it's natural for people to feel anxious about their livelihoods. This verse reminds us that all our labor, when done with diligence and integrity, can be an offering to Yahweh, giving it enduring purpose beyond economic shifts. Even as job roles evolve, the dignity of human contribution...
reflection.zh: 随着人工智能等技术进步重塑工作世界，人们对生计感到焦虑是自然的。这节经文提醒我们，我们所有的劳动，只要勤勉正直地完成，都可以是献给雅伟的供物，使其超越经济变迁而拥有持久的意义。即使工作角色不断演变，人类贡献的尊严依然存在，植根于更高的呼召。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: The future of AI hinges on openness and cooperation. China and Britain can gain much by working together | Zheng Zeguang
title.zh: 人工智能的未来取决于开放与合作。中英两国携手合作可获益良多 | 郑泽光

summary.en: The Chinese ambassador to the UK, Zheng Zeguang, advocates for international cooperation between China and Britain in artificial intelligence development. He highlights the significant benefits of working together in areas such as manufacturing, healthcare, research, and governance, rather than competing in isolation.
summary.zh: 中国驻英国大使郑泽光呼吁中英两国在人工智能发展方面开展国际合作。他强调，两国在制造业、医疗保健、研究和治理等领域携手合作而非孤立竞争，将带来巨大的益处。

body.en: There is no point competing in isolation. There are so many benefits to be had, in manufacturing, healthcare, research and governance Zheng Zeguang is the Chinese ambassador to the UK Artificial intelligence is widely regarded as one of the defining technologies of our time. Like the steam engine, the harnessing of electricity and the internet before it, it has the potential to transform how we work, live and interact. title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

title.en: 'Steadfast advocate': Arnhem Land's Rirratjingu clan elder Bakamumu Marika dies
title.zh: “坚定的倡导者”：阿纳姆地Rirratjingu部落长老巴卡穆穆·马里卡去世

summary.en: Bakamumu Marika, a Rirratjingu clan elder from Arnhem Land, has passed away. He was known for his lifelong dedication to fighting for land rights and championing Indigenous people.
summary.zh: 阿纳姆地Rirratjingu部落长老巴卡穆穆·马里卡去世。他一生致力于为土地权利和原住民争取权益。

body.en:
A respected elder of Arnhem Land's Rirratjingu clan, Bakamumu Marika AM, has died, the clan group's Aboriginal corporation has announced.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Bakamumu Marika AM, a highly respected Traditional Owner, elder and senior leader of the Rirratjingu Clan," the statement said.

Marika was a founder, long-serving chairman and current patron of the Rirratjingu Aboriginal Corporation who was appointed a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) in 2022 for his significant community service to North-East Arnhem Land.

As a "steadfast advocate" for land rights, Marika continued one of the most significant legacies in Australia’s Indigenous rights history, honouring and advancing the work of his forefathers, the statement reads.

A proud Rirratjingu man, cultural custodian and champion for his people, Marika dedicated his life to advancing opportunities in education, community development, economic participation and cultural preservation.

His commitment to working collectively, guided by Yolŋu values and traditions, strengthened his community and inspired younger generations to take pride in their culture and identity.

"We honour Bakamumu Marika's legacy and will forever be guided by his own words: 'We must continue to strive for a foundation that provides opportunity for our people. You will carry that responsibility along with my wish that unity and love continue to be the mark of the Rirratjingu people. I say to you, as my father said to me — ‘stand strong like the rock, Mandula'."

The Yothu Yindi Foundation (YYF), host of the Garma Festival , also expressed condolences following Marika's passing.

"Mr Marika was a beloved Yolŋu leader who devoted his life to his family and his people.

"His father, Roy Dadaynga Marika, is regarded as a founder of land rights, a legacy that he continued.

"As the founder and long-serving chairman of the Rirratjiŋu Aboriginal Corporation, he advocated tirelessly for his clan and all Yolŋu."

title.en: Two people seriously injured as building collapses in inner Sydney
title.zh: 悉尼市中心一栋建筑倒塌，两人受重伤

summary.en: Two people have been transported to hospital in serious condition after a building collapsed in inner Sydney.

body.en:
Two people have been hospitalised after a building collapsed in central Sydney on Monday, emergency services said.

A spokesperson for New South Wales Ambulance said it was called to an address in Ultimo, a suburb around 2 km from the city's central business district, just before 11am.

Workers assessed seven patients at the scene. According to ABC News, one man in his 60s and another in his 30s were removed from the rubble and rushed to hospital in a serious condition.

One of the men was taken to St Vincent's Hospital Sydney. The other was taken to Royal Prince Alfred Hospital.

Fire and Rescue New South Wales (FRNSW) told ABC News that the building was a construction site. Nearby buildings, including an adjoining service station, have been evacuated.

title.en: 'Deeply saddened': Australian helicopter provider speaks after Greece firefighting tragedy
title.zh: “深感悲痛”：希腊消防悲剧后，澳大利亚直升机供应商发声

summary.en: McDermott Aviation, an Australian helicopter provider, has expressed profound sadness following a firefighting tragedy in Greece, where helicopters leased by the company were involved as wildfires continue to spread across southern Europe.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚直升机供应商麦克德莫特航空对希腊消防悲剧表示深切哀悼，该公司租赁的直升机参与了扑灭南欧持续蔓延的野火。

body.en:
Two crew members have died after two helicopters — leased by Australian company McDermott Aviation — collided midair while battling wildfires in Greece on Sunday.

A Greek and a Danish national were killed in the crash over Psatha, an area west of Athens, according to Greece's fire service. Two crew members from Greece and Britain who were operating a separate helicopter were found alive.

Founder and president of McDermott Aviation, John McDermott said he was "deeply saddened" by news of the fatal collision.

"We are deeply saddened to confirm that the two crew members aboard one of the helicopters have lost their lives. The two crew members from the second helicopter are in the care of medical professionals.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident. Both crews were undertaking the critical work of supporting firefighting operations to help protect communities."

McDermott Aviation has reportedly operated in Greece for several years. The company said it is working closely with relevant authorities as they undertake an investigation into the cause of the incident.

Over the past decade, McDermott Aviation said it has engaged in around 10 to 12 international movements a year via sea and air freight. It also operates in New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the United States, which is currently experiencing wildfires in several western states.

Nikos Pagiotelis has been a volunteer firefighter in Greece for more than 20 years. He told SBS Greek about the moment he heard news of the crash over local radio.

"When you are inside the fire, and you are trying to help the people, you're trying to save the animals, save the forest. Then suddenly [you] hear that two helicopters have crashed a couple of miles near you — you can understand that something really hurts inside," Pagiotelis said.

"You can do nothing, you freeze for a little bit, and then you just continue your work. You continue to help people to honour the lives of the loss of two comrades."

In a statement on social media, Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also expressed his "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the deceased firefighters.

"The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot at the time they were attempting the major fire in Porto Gremeno fills us all with grief," Mitsotakis said.

Nearly 500 firefighters and 23 aircraft have been deployed to fight fires in Greece, which have been driven by high temperatures and gale-force winds.

title.en: Big tech companies could be hit with higher taxes if they don't strike deals with publishers
title.zh: 如果大型科技公司不与出版商达成协议，它们可能会面临更高的税收

summary.en: Tech giants criticised the previous draft laws released in April. What's changed?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Tech firms will pay a higher levy or strike more deals to avoid the charge under planned tweaks to an initiative to force them to hand over some of their revenue to media companies.

The proposed news bargaining incentive will push companies like Google, Meta and TikTok to strike commercial deals with news organisations to use the publishers' content on their platforms.

If deals are struck, the companies will pay a smaller share of their Australian advertising revenues to the government than if they refuse to reach agreements.

The levy will apply to tech giants with domestic revenues of $250 million or more, with any funds raised to be redistributed to the media sector.

But after a consultation period on the changes, which Labor hopes to legislate when parliament returns in Spring, elements of the incentive have been tipped further in favour of news publishers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The maximum levy that tech companies will pay on their revenue has been increased from 2.5 per cent from a previously proposed 2.25 per cent charge, the government revealed on Monday.

They will also have to strike at least six deals with publishers — rather than four — to fully discharge the liability.

But the revenue used to calculate the tech giants' payments will be limited to digital advertising income attributable to the Australian market.

Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino said the government had shown good faith in negotiating with both the platforms and media companies during the consultation process.

"Australian journalism is important to a well-functioning democracy and we want it to be sustainable now and into the future," he said.

"We want digital platforms to do deals with a diverse range of media organisations."

Approved agreements with large media companies would allow tech companies to offset 150 per cent of their liabilities, while deals with smaller firms attract a 200 per cent offset — up from 170 per cent under previous plans.

A professional networking platform carve-out that would have excluded LinkedIn has been scrapped.

The previous draft laws, released in April, were heavily criticised by the tech giants as "a government-mandated transfer of wealth from one industry to another".

title.en: Home prices fall across Australia as housing downturn takes hold
title.zh: 澳大利亚房价下跌，楼市低迷

summary.en: National home prices recorded their biggest monthly decline since 2022, with Sydney and Melbourne leading the falls.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚全国房价录得自2022年以来的最大月度跌幅，其中悉尼和墨尔本领跌。

body.en:
Australia's housing market downturn is spreading across the country as higher interest rates and changes to property taxes take hold.

Figures from property analytics company Cotality showed national home prices fell 0.7 per cent last month, the largest single-month decline since December 2022.

Annual growth has slowed to 5.3 per cent, well below the double-digit pace recorded earlier this year.

The country's largest property markets, Sydney and Melbourne, recorded declines of 1.4 per cent and 1.2 per cent respectively. Both cities are more than five per cent lower than recent peaks.

Brisbane and Adelaide, where prices have recently boomed, also recorded drops of 0.6 and 0.2 per cent respectively.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In Perth, which has recorded the strongest year-on-year growth of any capital city at 21.8 per cent , prices were virtually flat, rising just 0.1 per cent.

"For buyers who remain in the market, lower competition and elevated stock levels (when compared with the start of the year) mean greater choice and more negotiating power," the property analytics firm said.

However, the fall in prices has been led by properties at the higher end of the market, providing little benefit to first home-buyers who are also grappling with lower borrowing capacity after three interest rate hikes this year.

Homes in the top quarter of the market lost 3.2 per cent of their value in the three months to July, compared to a 0.3 per cent gain in the lower-price tier.

Beyond the capital cities, the regional property market recorded a drop a 0.2 per cent — the first decline since January 2023.

"There remains a mismatch between the pricing expectations of buyers and sellers," Cotality head of research Gerard Burg said.

Consumer sentiment has also been soured by high living costs, uncertainty caused by the ongoing Middle East war and tax changes announced in the May budget.

"We have observed a deterioration in the flow of new listings across the country in recent weeks, led by Sydney, as potential vendors assess a weak market and choose to wait until conditions improve," Burg said.

Rental prices have continued to rise due to low vacancy rates. Burg said national median rents had risen by more than $200 a week in the last five years.

"Despite the tight market conditions, there are question marks about how much further rents can rise," he said.

body.zh: 随着利率上升和财产税的变化，澳大利亚房地产市场的低迷正在全国蔓延。 房地产分析公司 Cotality 的数据显示，上个月全国房价下跌 0.7%，这是自 2022 年 12 月以来的最大单月跌幅。 年增长率已放缓至 5.3%，远低于今年早些时候录得的两位数增速。 该国最大的房地产市场悉尼和墨尔本分别下跌1.4%和1.2%。这两个城市的房价都比最近的峰值低了百分之五以上。 最近房价上涨的布里斯班和阿德莱德也分别下跌了0.6%和0.2%。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 珀斯的同比增长率为所有首府城市中最强劲的，达到 21.8%，但价格几乎持平，仅上涨 0.1%。 该房地产分析公司表示：“对于留在市场上的买家来说，竞争的减少和库存水平的提高（与年初相比）意味着更多的选择和更强的谈判能力。” 然而，价格下跌是由高端市场的房地产带动的，这对首次购房者几乎没有什么好处，他们在今年三次加息后也面临着借贷能力下降的问题。 截至 7 月份的三个月内，高端市场四分之一的房屋价值下跌了 3.2%，而低价位房屋的价值则上涨了 0.3%。 除首府城市外，地区房地产市场下跌 0.2%，这是自 2023 年 1 月以来的首次下跌。 Cotality 研究主管 Gerard Burg 表示：“买家和卖家的定价预期仍然不匹配。” 高昂的生活成本、持续不断的中东战争造成的不确定性以及五月份预算中宣布的税收变化也削弱了消费者信心。 伯格表示：“我们观察到，最近几周，以悉尼为首的全国新挂牌房源数量出现恶化，因为潜在的卖家评估了疲软的市场，并选择等待情况好转。” 由于空置率较低，租金价格持续上涨。 Burg 表示，过去 5 年全国平均租金每周上涨超过 200 美元。 他表示：“尽管市场状况紧张，但租金还能进一步上涨多少仍存在疑问。” 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: A downturn in housing prices can bring financial uncertainty and remind us that earthly treasures are not permanent. This news invites us to consider where our true security and hope lie, beyond fluctuating markets and material possessions.
reflection.zh: 房价下跌可能带来财务上的不确定性，并提醒我们地上的财宝并非永恒。这则新闻邀请我们思考，我们真正的安全和盼望，超越了波动的市场和物质财富，究竟在哪里。

verse.textEn: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy.
verse.textZh: 不要为自己积攒财宝在地上；地上有虫子咬，能锈坏。
